newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says all opposition detainees freed.
newsitem.headline: Burma says all opposition detainees freed.

text.p: Burma said on Tuesday it had released the last batch of 63 detainees being held after a recent crackdown on activists of Aung San Suu Kyi's opposition National League for Democracy Party (NLD).
They were the last of a total of 573 NLD party members and supporters who were detained to prevent the NLD from holding a party congress at the end of September.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) had deemed the congress illegal and barrred access to Suu Kyi's home where the meeting was to be held from September 26.
The latest release was announced on state-owned television. Authorities have freed the detainees in stages since last week.
On Tuesday, police also lifted checkpoints erected on University Avenue to stop access to Suu Kyi's home.
Since public access to her home was barred, the democracy leader had been unable to hold weekend public gatherings in front of her home for two consecutive weekends.
She told a news conference on Tuesday that she was now ready to resume the weekend gatherings again.
